questions.q: What does lesson 1 say successful marketers do?
a: Tell stories people want to believe

questions.q: What does George Riedel's story say about wine glasses?
a: The glass is the interpreter of the wine's story
questions.why: Lesson 1 says each wine has a story that the glass translates.

questions.q: Why do we believe stories, according to lesson 2?
a: Our brains compare only what's new, not all features
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses the frog and iPhone examples.

questions.q: What is the difference between a fib and fraud, per lesson 3?
a: A fib improves the experience; fraud hurts authenticity
A fib is illegal; fraud isn't
A fib is about price; fraud about quality

questions.q: What example shows an overpriced product's perceived value?
a: Nike shoes that cost little to make but sell for much more
